jp: このペンは軽[かる]くて書[か]き{やすい|pt-yasui}です。
en: This pen is light and easy to write with.
why: 軽くて points to an advantage, so 〜やすい (easy to do) fits.

jp: 先生[せんせい]の説明[せつめい]は分[わ]かり{やすい|pt-yasui}ので、みんな好[す]きです。
en: The teacher's explanations are easy to understand, so everyone likes them.
why: Everyone likes them, so the explanations are easy to understand: 〜やすい.

jp: 冬[ふゆ]は空気[くうき]が乾燥[かんそう]しているので、風邪[かぜ]をひき{やすい|pt-yasui}です。
en: In winter the air is dry, so it is easy to catch a cold.
why: 〜やすい also means tends to happen; dry air makes colds likely.

jp: この道[みち]は雨[あめ]の日[ひ]に滑[すべ]り{やすい|pt-yasui}から、気[き]をつけてください。
en: This road is slippery on rainy days, so please be careful.
why: The warning only makes sense if slipping is likely: 〜やすい.

jp: 駅[えき]に近[ちか]くて、とても住[す]み{やすい|pt-yasui}町[まち]です。
en: It is a town close to the station and very easy to live in.
why: Being close to the station makes the town comfortable to live in: 〜やすい.

jp: この辞書[じしょ]は字[じ]が大[おお]きくて、見[み]{やすい|pt-yasui}です。
en: This dictionary has large print and is easy to read.
why: Large print makes it easy to see: 〜やすい.

jp: 暗[くら]い所[ところ]で本[ほん]を読[よ]むと、目[め]が疲[つか]れ{やすい|pt-yasui}です。
en: If you read in a dark place, your eyes tire easily.
why: Eyes getting tired is a tendency that is likely to occur: 〜やすい.

jp: ひらがなは漢字[かんじ]より覚[おぼ]え{やすい|pt-yasui}です。
en: Hiragana is easier to remember than kanji.
why: Comparing hiragana favourably with kanji gives 〜やすい.

jp: この靴[くつ]は軽[かる]くて、歩[ある]き{やすかった|pt-yasui}です。
en: These shoes were light and easy to walk in.
why: Light shoes are easy to walk in; the past form is やすかった.

jp: 彼[かれ]は怒[おこ]り{やすい|pt-yasui}人[ひと]なので、話[はな]すときに気[き]をつけています。
en: He is a person who gets angry easily, so I am careful when I talk to him.
why: Being careful makes sense because he tends to get angry: 〜やすい.

jp: この会社[かいしゃ]は働[はたら]き{やすくて|pt-yasui}、友[とも]だちにも勧[すす]めたいです。
en: This company is easy to work at, and I want to recommend it to my friends too.
why: Wanting to recommend it means it is a pleasant place to work: やすくて.

jp: 古[ふる]い建物[たてもの]は、地震[じしん]で壊[こわ]れ{やすい|pt-yasui}と言[い]われています。
en: It is said that old buildings are easily damaged by earthquakes.
why: Old buildings are more likely to break in an earthquake: 〜やすい.

jp: この車[くるま]は小[ちい]さくて、運転[うんてん]し{やすい|pt-yasui}です。
en: This car is small and easy to drive.
why: Being small is an advantage when driving: 〜やすい.

jp: 梅雨[つゆ]は食[た]べ物[もの]が腐[くさ]り{やすい|pt-yasui}ので、冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]に入[い]れてください。
en: In the rainy season food goes bad easily, so please put it in the fridge.
why: The advice to refrigerate makes sense because food spoils easily: 〜やすい.

jp: このコップは持[も]ち{やすい|pt-yasui}形[かたち]で、子[こ]どもにも使[つか]えます。
en: This cup has a shape that is easy to hold, so children can use it too.
why: Children can use it because it is easy to hold: 〜やすい.

jp: この漢字[かんじ]は小[ちい]さくて、読[よ]み{にくい/づらい|pt-yasui}です。
en: This kanji is small and hard to read.
why: Small print is hard to read, so 〜にくい (hard to do) is needed.

jp: この靴[くつ]は固[かた]くて、歩[ある]き{にくい/づらい|pt-yasui}です。
en: These shoes are stiff and hard to walk in.
why: Stiff shoes make walking difficult: 〜にくい.

jp: 友[とも]だちには、ちょっと言[い]い{にくい/づらい|pt-yasui}ことがあります。
en: There is something that is a bit hard to say to my friend.
why: Something awkward to bring up is 言いにくい.

jp: この肉[にく]は硬[かた]くて、食[た]べ{にくい/づらい|pt-yasui}です。
en: This meat is tough and hard to eat.
why: Tough meat is difficult to eat: 〜にくい.

jp: このガラスは丈夫[じょうぶ]で、落[お]としても割[わ]れ{にくい|pt-yasui}です。
en: This glass is sturdy and does not break easily even if you drop it.
why: Sturdy glass is unlikely to break, so 〜にくい (does not tend to) is needed.

jp: このシャツは汚[よご]れが付[つ]き{にくい|pt-yasui}ので、白[しろ]でも安心[あんしん]です。
en: Dirt does not stick to this shirt easily, so even a white one is no worry.
why: 安心 only makes sense if dirt is unlikely to stick: 〜にくい (does not tend to).

jp: 毎日[まいにち]運動[うんどう]をしているので、私[わたし]は太[ふと]り{にくい|pt-yasui}です。
en: Because I exercise every day, I do not put on weight easily.
why: Daily exercise makes weight gain less likely: 〜にくい.

jp: 前[まえ]の人[ひと]の頭[あたま]が大[おお]きくて、スクリーンが見[み]{にくかった/づらかった|pt-yasui}です。
en: The person in front had a big head, so the screen was hard to see.
why: A big head blocking the view makes the screen hard to see: 〜にくかった.

jp: この地域[ちいき]は、冬[ふゆ]でも雪[ゆき]が降[ふ]り{にくい|pt-yasui}です。
en: In this area it rarely snows, even in winter.
why: 冬でも (even in winter) only works if snow is unlikely: 〜にくい (does not tend to happen).

jp: 彼[かれ]は気持[きも]ちを顔[かお]に出[だ]さないので、何[なに]を考[かんが]えているか分[わ]かり{にくい/づらい|pt-yasui}です。
en: He does not show his feelings, so it is hard to tell what he is thinking.
why: Not showing feelings makes his thoughts hard to understand: 〜にくい.

jp: この薬[くすり]は苦[にが]くて、子[こ]どもには飲[の]み{にくい/づらい|pt-yasui}です。
en: This medicine is bitter and hard for children to take.
why: Bitterness makes it difficult to swallow: 〜にくい.

jp: このペンは細[ほそ]すぎて、持[も]ち{にくい/づらい|pt-yasui}です。
en: This pen is too thin and is hard to hold.
why: A pen that is too thin is hard to grip: 〜にくい.

jp: この電車[でんしゃ]は混[こ]んでいて、降[お]り{にくい/づらい|pt-yasui}ですね。
en: This train is crowded, so it is hard to get off, isn't it?
why: A crowded train makes getting off difficult: 〜にくい.

jp: このフライパンは新[あたら]しいので、卵[たまご]が焦[こ]げ{にくい|pt-yasui}です。
en: This frying pan is new, so eggs do not burn onto it easily.
why: A new non-stick pan makes burning unlikely: 〜にくい.

jp: うちの犬[いぬ]は病気[びょうき]になり{にくい|pt-yasui}と、獣医[じゅうい]さんが言[い]っていました。
en: The vet said that our dog is not likely to get sick.
why: A healthy dog is unlikely to fall ill: 〜にくい.
